card.keepWhy: One more try, out in the deep.
sources: Luke 5:1-3 (crowd at the lake of Gennesaret, i.e. the Sea of Galilee; fishermen washing nets; Jesus teaches from Simon’s boat)
Luke 5:4 (“Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch”)
Luke 5:5 (“Master, we worked all night and caught nothing; but at your word I will let down the net”)
Luke 5:6-7 (nets begin to break; partners in the other boat come; both boats fill and begin to sink)
Luke 5:8 (“Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord”)
Luke 5:10 (James and John, sons of Zebedee, Simon’s partners; “Don’t be afraid. From now on you will be catching people”)
Luke 5:11 (they left everything and followed him)
Related, not used in captions: John 21:1-11 (a second night of empty nets and a full catch after the resurrection)
Luke 5:9 (amazement seized him and all who were with him)

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever worked all night, or all year, and had nothing to show for it?
options: then sit with me a minute. this one starts right there.
then you’ll know how simon felt. listen.
good. keep this one for the next long night.

steps.line: Simon was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee. He’d fished all night and caught nothing. Now he was on the shore, washing his nets.
A crowd pressed in to hear Jesus. He stepped into Simon’s boat, asked him to push out a little, and taught from there.

steps.q: When he finishes teaching, Jesus sends Simon back out to fish. Where?
steps.why: Into the deep, in broad daylight, after a whole night of nothing (Luke 5:4). Any fisherman on that lake would have shaken his head.

steps.line: “Put out into the deep water, and let down your nets for a catch.”
steps.label: Luke 5:4

steps.pre: “Master, we worked all night and caught nothing. But
steps.why: “Because you say so.” He’s tired, he knows the lake better than any teacher, and he does it anyway.

steps.q: Simon lets the nets down in broad daylight. What happens?
o: A decent catch, worth the trouble
So many fish the nets tear
steps.why: Galilee fishermen worked at night, when fish can’t see the nets. In daylight, the nets began to break, and it took two boats to hold the catch.

steps.line: The nets filled until they began to tear. They signaled to their partners, James and John, and both boats filled until they began to sink.
Simon fell at Jesus’s knees. “Go away from me, Lord. I’m a sinful man.”
steps.label: Luke 5:8

steps.q: Simon just had the best catch of his life. Why does he say “go away from me”?
o: He was angry the nets had torn
He felt unworthy to be near him
He was afraid the boats would sink
steps.why: Luke says amazement seized him. Up close to something holy, Simon felt small. Watch how gently Jesus answers.

steps.line: Jesus said, “Don’t be afraid. From now on you’ll be catching people.”
steps.label: Luke 5:10

steps.line: They brought the boats to shore, left everything, and followed him.

steps.q: “You’ll be catching people.” Luke’s Greek word is unusual for fishing. What does it mean?
steps.why: Zōgrōn: taking alive. Fish in a net were caught to die; the people Simon would gather were caught to live.

say: here’s what i love. simon knew fishing better than any teacher. he said so. then he let the nets down anyway.
christians read it as a picture of trust: “because you say so.” peter’s fresh start began with one more try he didn’t feel like making.

steps.q: After Easter, John’s Gospel tells a catch very like this one, with Peter again. One detail flips. Which?
o: This time the net doesn’t tear
This time Jesus does the fishing
steps.why: John 21: a hundred and fifty-three large fish, “and the net was not torn.” Same lake, same Peter, a second fresh start after he’d denied Jesus three times.

today.say: pick one thing you’ve given up on: a habit, a goal, a conversation. many christians bring it to God first, a short prayer or a quiet moment, if you’d like. then give it one more honest try, the way simon did: “because you say so.”
options: that’s the whole story. nets out one more time.
that counts. simon explained first too. then he went.
